speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: On 22 October 2024 at about 5.08 pm, a Bukit Panjang Light Rail Transit, or BPLRT, train moving in the direction of Choa Chu Kang station stalled before Teck Whye station.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: To preserve service along the affected stretch, SMRT activated a shuttle train service using the other bound of track between Bukit Panjang and Choa Chu Kang LRT stations at 5.19 pm.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: SMRT also activated free regular bus services to provide commuters with another alternative travel option between the affected stations.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: BPLRT loop services between Bukit Panjang and Petir stations via Service A, and between Bukit Panjang and Senja stations via Service B, were not affected and continued throughout the evening.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: In accordance with standard operating procedure, SMRT deployed an empty recovery train to couple with the stalled train.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: To ensure commuter safety, all passengers on the incident train disembarked onto the station platform at Teck Whye station by 5.40 pm.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Thereafter, the recovery train proceeded to move the empty incident train back towards the BPLRT depot, where further checks could be done.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: During this movement, a power trip occurred and the coupled trains stalled due to a loss of traction power.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As a consequence, the pair of wheels on the damaged wheel assembly were unable to rotate normally.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As the affected wheels on the incident train were unable to rotate, the friction between the rubber tyres and the guideway caused the tyres to deflate.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This then resulted in a bar below the carriage of the incident train to come into contact with the power rail, which caused damage to the power rail and led to the power trip.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For the safety of commuters and repair workers, SMRT assessed that recovery works on the stalled train and damaged power rail should only take place after the affected stretch of the BPLRT is shut down.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Free bus services between the affected stations continued until 1.00 am.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: SMRT carried out repair works throughout the night.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Thorough checks were then conducted to ensure safety before BPLRT services resumed at 5.00 am the following morning.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Edward Chia and Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked about the progress of BPLRT renewal works and the resumption of double loop service.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: First, LTA is bringing in new trains and upgrading existing ones.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Second, we are upgrading all the BPLRT core systems such as power and signalling.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We have four new third-generation vehicles that have entered passenger service, with another two currently undergoing testing.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The remaining 13 new vehicles will arrive progressively over the coming year.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The second-generation vehicles are also being enhanced – six of these have completed their upgrades and are in passenger service, while the remaining seven will be progressively upgraded over the next 12 months.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We target for the new and upgraded vehicles to enter service by end-2025.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The power supply system for the BPLRT has been fully upgraded with increased capacity, including enhancements such as dedicated power supply monitoring and control systems.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: LTA is currently upgrading the Operations Control Centre and replacing the power rails to improve operations and system reliability.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: When in operation, the new signalling system will allow better control of train speeds, so that commuters can enjoy smoother and more reliable rides.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We have fully resumed dual-loop services on BPLRT for all hours on weekends and public holidays since 28 September 2024.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: LTA aims to resume dual-loop services for all hours on weekdays in the coming months.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We are on track to complete the BPLRT renewal programme in 2026.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We recognise that the improvement works have been a long journey, but we have to go through this process to fix the legacy problems and deliver better service for our commuters.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We thank commuters and residents for their understanding and patience during this period when we are carrying out the renewal programme.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: When completed in 2026, the upgraded BPLRT will provide commuters with a more reliable, more comfortable and smoother travel experience.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: First, SMRT has formed a tripartite Rail Safety and Reliability Review Workgroup to review its systems and processes, including its maintenance practices and lifecycle management of assets.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: SMRT has invited representatives from LTA and the National Transport Workers' Union (NTWU) to join this Workgroup and will also engage overseas metro operators in Guangzhou and Taipei for mutual learning.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: LTA welcomes this initiative and will work together with SMRT and NTWU in this tripartite workgroup to identify areas for improvement and maintain safety and reliability standards for the benefit of commuters.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Importantly, all the MRT lines have continued to achieve our target MKBF of at least one million train-kilometres.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is a priority for the One Transport Family.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is our common mission and our shared goal, and we will work closely together and do our best to achieve it.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, maybe my first question for the Minister is whether he can give us a clearer timeline, instead of just saying the coming months.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: And if, indeed, there could be more risks, how can LTA and SMRT be better prepared for this very critical phase and also to reduce any inconveniences to our commuters should there be any disruption?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If I could give him a more specific date, I would be happy to do so.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But I think it is important for us to monitor the progress closely.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And along the way, we will certainly provide updates to Mr Liang and to the other grassroots advisors who are looking after the Bukit Panjang area.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But we want to do so in a manner which is safe for the workers and also for commuters.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Liang also asked about the services and the reliability during this period.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Indeed, this upgrading journey has been a long one and it involves bringing in new trains, upgrading existing trains, as well as upgrading all the BPLRT core systems, such as power and signalling.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And because it is done on multiple fronts, we need to make sure that this is done safely and, to make it even more challenging, because you have to run the BPLRT services during the operating or revenue hours, we could only do some of the maintenance and some of these works during the engineering hours.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, that is why we seek the understanding of our residents and commuters, that we will need to have early closure during this period to give more time for the upgrading works to be completed.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I want to also assure Mr Liang that commuter safety is a top priority.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That is why we want to plan the renewal works very carefully and to cater for thorough and comprehensive testing.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And we will certainly try to do so with minimal impact on the existing BPLRT operations so that the renewed BPLRT system will become even better and the rides will be more reliable, smoother, more comfortable for commuters.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: During the early closure, we will also put up information, such as posters, at the affected stations to inform commuters of the service adjustments.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And there will be public address announcements in the stations and trains to remind passengers to make alternative travel arrangements, if needed.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: To Mr Liang's other question, we will certainly do our best to ensure that the testing and the integration works can proceed smoothly and as planned.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And if, touch wood, we were to experience any disruptions during this period, we will certainly do our best to respond quickly and effectively.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The rail operators have in place robust response plans in the event of a service disruption.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These include the incident recovery procedures as well as the provision of alternative transportation options, such as free buses, that will serve the journey between the affected stations.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And we will certainly take on board the learning points from past incidents and also when we do exercises and reviews that can help LTA and our operators to be able to make continual improvements to our incident response plans.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And this will include the timeliness and clarity of our public announcements in the event of a disruption and also how we can better manage the crowd that will be affected during the disruptions.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And we are grateful to commuters and to residents for their kind understanding and patience during this period because our end outcome is something that I hope will lead to a more reliable, safer and more comfortable ride for our commuters.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In the investigations done, was there a root cause analysis done to ensure that there were no systemic issues with the breakdown?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And given that there will be new dual-carriage trains coming into the Punggol LRT loop next year, what updates to the maintenance and checks standard operating procedures will be added?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And what measures have been taken to ensure that our engineers and station operators are sufficiently trained to ensure that they are safe during repair works?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I cannot quite give a definite answer on what is the root cause.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I have explained what we have gathered so far in my main reply.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But if we look at the past track record of the BPLRT, the last time we had a similar incident that affected the gears of the wheel assembly was in 2010.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, that was quite some time ago and it has not recurred since.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, this more recent episode, we will have to look into exactly what was the root cause.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But I think it does not suggest that there is something systemic in this particular instance.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We will take a look more closely during the investigations.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These trains will undergo rigorous testing and commissioning before they are put into passenger service starting from the second half of 2025.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Indeed, I think we are aiming to see how we can do better with the system upgrades and also the train upgrades.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: With a better signalling system, we can certainly run the trains with a higher frequency and that will then help to cater more capacity for our commuters.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But we have to go through a period of the upgrading works before we are able to arrive at that outcome.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I want to thank Mr Chia as well for working with us to explain the situation to his residents and also to continue to share the feedback from the residents with LTA.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Just to confirm with the Minister that the one million-threshold for MKBF was set a number of years ago, about five years ago now.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The Minister shared some data of the reliability of certain lines and that reliability figure has obviously gone higher than one million MKBF.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Can I confirm whether the Ministry of Transport is considering raising the threshold and, if it does, what would be the reasons why it would do so and whether it is sustainable going forward.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: At the moment, I think that one million is still a relevant and valid target, and that is something that the One Transport Family will work towards, will continue to maintain, to ensure that our system can keep above this one million target.
